mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate at or below 0.1% indicates an ultra-accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS <= 0.1%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate exceeding 6.0% signals a weakening labor market that may lead to a recession, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE > 6.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment (PAYEMS < 140,000) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE > 6.0%) signals a labor market contraction that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS < 140000 and UNRATE > 6.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime characterized by a housing market boom (HOUST > 1100 thousand units) and robust consumer spending (RSAFS > 440,000 million dollars), the S&P 500 tends to produce positive returns over the next 60 trading days as the economy approaches its peak.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST > 1100 and RSAFS > 440000, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
